NovaLearn may officially state that the Microsoft Teams connector is **not generally available** and is currently in the **design and planning phase**, with a release target of **Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)** [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. This status is confirmed across official documentation, which lists the integration as "in the design phase for Q4 2026" [NL-001#NL-001-S08] and explicitly states it is "currently not generally available" [NL-002#NL-002-S11]. The official support guidance also instructs that the integration is in the design phase for Q4 2026 [NL-006#NL-006-S07] and is under active design to ensure security compliance [NL-007#NL-007-S08].

NovaLearn must reject the lower-authority claim that the connector is "basically ready," "almost ready," or "right around the corner," as made by the sales representative in the internal sales call [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. This is a significant sales overclaim contradicted by the official roadmap [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. The internal Slack thread further confirms the project is merely a basic proof-of-concept webhook demo with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO integration, and zero formatting/citation links, making it far from ready for customer deployment [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. The official roadmap explicitly flags these sales and Slack communications as contradictions that CSMs must clarify [NL-014#NL-014-S07].
